items.title: Podcasts about the Topic: Part II
items.summary:
With Curt Jaimungal:

The title Curt put next to my head could’ve been in reference to many, many things! But sorry, he just mean AI. He and I start with the Mathacre , of course, but then we get onto the firewall paradox and then Curt starts asking about computational complexity and the Second Law, and then about Integrated Information Theory .

OK, despite the title of this post, short break from “The Topic.” Here’s an absolute masterpiece of mathematical exposition, from the “Polylog” YouTube channel, which tells the story of the determination of Busy Beaver values through spectacular animations. I play cameo roles in the video, although I embarrass myself (as the video silently points out) by transposing two digits in the value of BB(5)…!

And, coming soon (not on YouTube quite yet): a conversation about the Mathacre with celebrated physics popularizer (and character on The Big Bang Theory ) Brian Greene , recorded in-person in NYC during my recent trip to speak in the math department at Columbia University!

And to preempt the inevitable comments about it: yes , my students just came to my office to tell me that an OpenAI model has now refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis , by giving an algorithm to solve 3SAT in an amount of time that scales roughly like exp(n/√log(n)). Even as we struggle to digest the previous courses, the endless buffet continues!

items.title: Intel to Acquire Classiq to Create a Full-stack Quantum Computing Platform
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Intel has agreed to acquire quantum software company Classiq, combining its algorithm synthesis platform with Intel’s silicon spin-qubit hardware and software to build a full-stack quantum computing business.

Classiq’s platform automates quantum circuit design, enabling developers to create applications without deep expertise in the underlying hardware.

The acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and customary conditions, with Intel planning to maintain Classiq’s support for multiple hardware platforms.

PRESS RELEASE — Intel Corporation today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Classiq, a leading provider of quantum computing software. The combination of Classiq’s synthesis platform with Intel’s spin-qubit manufacturing and existing software would create a user-friendly full-stack quantum computing platform, enabling the promising technology to mature into a mainstream computing business.

More than forty years ago, the invention of Electronic Design Automation (EDA) and Computer‑Aided Design (CAD) software transformed silicon chip design and classical computing by providing a common software platform that could abstract the ability to design chips from the complexity of the underlying hardware. Classiq plays a similar role in quantum computing, providing a unifying software platform that is agnostic to the underlying qubit modality and hardware. Providing this high-level abstraction enables quantum computing to scale beyond custom hand-crafted circuits and applications to become a mainstream computing platform.

Classiq’s synthesis platform brings complementary assets to Intel’s already strong quantum hardware and software capabilities developed over the last decade. Since 2015, Intel has been investing in the development of quantum computing, and today it is the only company capable of producing qubit chips and complex cryogenic control electronics at-scale, using equipment and processes common to conventional silicon-based semiconductor manufacturing.

items.title: IDEMIA Secure Transactions Collaborates With KT in Advancing Post-Quantum Security For South Korea’s Defense Communications
items.summary:
Insider Brief

IDEMIA Secure Transactions is collaborating with KT on a South Korean government-backed pilot to test SIM-based post-quantum cryptography for defense communications.

IDEMIA is implementing NIST-standardized and Korean algorithms on its Quantum-Resistant SIM platform, with a potential Korean smart-card first subject to final validation.

KT’s broader pilot will assess post-quantum security across defense systems, including PCs, surveillance equipment, drones and 5G networks.

Image: Photo by Daniel Bernard on Unsplash

PRESS RELEASE — IDEMIA Secure Transactions (IST), a global leader in payment, connectivity and cybersecurity, is collaborating with KT, a major South Korean mobile network operator, on South Korea’s 2026 Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Pilot Conversion Project. The project is organized by the Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) and the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA).

As part of the initiative, with KT playing a leading role, IST is implementing NIST-standardized and Korean PQC algorithms on the Quantum-Resistant SIM equipped smart-card platform to support the protection of defense communications systems against emerging cryptographic threats.

items.title: Israel Ranks Fourth in Private Quantum Investment as Sector Expands, According to Report
items.summary:
Insider Brief

A report by the Israel Innovation Authority and C4IR Israel finds that Israel’s quantum sector grew from about five companies and 50 employees in 2019 to more than 20 companies and roughly 1,000 employees in 2025.

Israeli quantum companies raised nearly $500 million in 2025, representing approximately 9% of global private quantum investment and ranking Israel fourth worldwide.

The report recommends targeted investment in Israel’s technological strengths, stronger international partnerships and broader industry adoption, with a proposed 2027–2031 national initiative supporting infrastructure and workforce development.

PRESS RELEASE — A new report by the Israel Innovation Authority and C4IR Israel (which operates within the Israel Innovation Authority and is part of the World Economic Forum’s global C4IR Network), was released today, titled “ Israel’s Quantum Ecosystem: Making Quantum Leaps Through Strategic Investment .” The report examines the rapid development of Israel’s quantum technology ecosystem, particularly quantum computing technologies and the distinctive innovation model supporting its growth.

The report finds that Israel has evolved within 6 years from a budding quantum industry into a highly concentrated and globally connected innovation ecosystem. The number of active Israeli quantum companies grew from approximately 5 in 2019 to more than 20 by 2025, while employment in quantum companies increased from approximately 50 to around 1,000 employees. In quantum computing alone, the number of companies increased from 1 to more than 10 during this period.

Private investment has accelerated accordingly. In 2025 alone, Israeli quantum companies raised nearly $500 million, equivalent to approximately 9% of global private investment in quantum technologies and approximately 15% when the United States is excluded. Israel ranked fourth globally in total private quantum investment, after the United States, United Kingdom and Canada.

items.title: Quantum Art Research Outlines More Efficient Quantum Approach to Wave Modeling
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Quantum Art presented research on a quantum algorithm that uses known wave physics to simplify large-scale wave simulations, with potential applications in telecommunications, seismic modeling and engineering.

The method constructs physically allowed wave states directly, aiming to avoid computational overhead that limits existing quantum approaches as the modeled region grows.

The company estimates that some simulations requiring 10¹⁸–10²¹ classical grid points could potentially use roughly 100 qubits, although practical implementation depends on further hardware advances.

PRESS RELEASE — – Quantum Art , a developer of full-stack, fault tolerant quantum computers based on trapped-ion qubits and a proprietary, dynamically reconfigurable multi-core architecture, recently presented new research, detailed in this paper , that solves wave-propagation problems long thought intractable for classical supercomputers – unlocking new simulation capabilities for seismic modeling, structural engineering, and materials science.

Simulating how waves, from radio signals to sound, travel through space demands enormous computing power, and that demand grows sharply when the area being modeled gets larger but the level of detail cannot be reduced. The stakes are real for industries that depend on precision: telecom carriers predict network coverage, engineers model how buildings and materials hold up under stress, and geophysicists track how seismic waves move through the earth. The research explains the science behind the large-scale wave-simulation results the company previously demonstrated in May through a joint project with a leading Israeli governmental research and development agency.

Quantum computers hold a key advantage here: they can represent extremely large problems using relatively few qubits. Most existing quantum methods, however, treat a wave problem as a vast, generic mathematical puzzle. They solve a huge system of equations by brute force, with little regard for what the equations describe. Waves follow strict physical rules: a wave of a given frequency travels at a fixed speed in a given medium, so every direction it could possibly travel in can be pictured as the hand of a clock. Because the speed is fixed, every hand is the same length, so their tips can only trace out one perfect circle. Anything off that circle is physically impossible. Prior methods still expend effort searching far outside that circle, checking possibilities that the physics has already ruled out. As a result, they tend to slow dramatically or lose their quantum advantage, especially on a large-scale problem.

items.title: Report: UK’s £30 Million Quantum Testbed Program Helps Suppliers Advance Toward Commercial Deployment
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Britain’s £30 million quantum computing testbed program helped seven suppliers deploy prototype systems across five computing approaches, gaining experience in installation, operation and customer support.

The initiative supported hardware development, new supplier partnerships and expanded UK operations, with collaborative projects securing £4.6 million in follow-on funding.

Six testbeds entered independent technical evaluation, with the main testing program due to conclude in the second quarter of 2027 to assess performance and explore potential applications.

Britain’s £30 million quantum computing testbed program helped seven hardware suppliers develop systems for use outside their own laboratories, offering lessons in installation, reliability and customer support as the country begins a broader evaluation of the machines, according to a new report.

The National Quantum Computing Centre’s Phase 1 report , released recently, identifies its role as an early customer as a central benefit of the initiative. Suppliers received funding and technical support, but also faced the practical demands of delivering working equipment, documenting its operation and preparing it for outside scrutiny.

The program established seven prototype systems across five approaches to quantum computing at the Harwell Campus in Oxfordshire. Its next phase, conducted with the University of Edinburgh ’s Quantum Software Lab, is evaluating performance and exploring which systems may suit particular computational problems.

items.title: Ramdeobaba University and QClairvoyance Quantum Labs to Set Up Quantum Software and Quantum Communication Labs in Nagpur
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Ramdeobaba University and QClairvoyance Quantum Labs signed an agreement to establish quantum software and quantum communication hardware laboratories at the university’s Nagpur campus.

The laboratories will provide browser-based tools for developing quantum algorithms and hardware kits for quantum key distribution and quantum random number generation.

QClairvoyance will assign two qualified professionals to the university for 12 months, provide faculty training and support joint research, academic projects and internships.

Image: Photo by Onkarphoto on Unsplash

PRESS RELEASE — Ramdeobaba University (RBU), Nagpur, and QClairvoyance Quantum Labs Pvt. Ltd., a deep-tech startup based in Secunderabad, have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish two specialised laboratories on the RBU campus: a quantum software lab and a quantum communication hardware lab.

The initiative aims to bring emerging quantum technologies into the classroom, giving students and faculty hands-on access to quantum computing and next-generation secure communication technologies. Through practical learning and research exposure, the collaboration will help students develop the skills and knowledge needed to understand and work with these technologies as they evolve.

items.title: Qubit’s Own Electric Current Could Offer a Simpler Readout Method
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Researchers proposed a method for reading Andreev qubits through their own oscillating supercurrent, potentially reducing measurement disturbance and eliminating auxiliary qubits.

The approach would use a sensitive magnetic detector to track the current and reconstruct the qubit’s state without requiring repeated resets.

Simulations reported reconstruction accuracies of 99.52% to 99.85%, but the proposed setup has yet to be tested experimentally.

Image: Photo by A Chosen Soul on Unsplash

PRESS RELEASE — One of the fundamental challenges of quantum computing is obtaining information from a quantum bit, or qubit. Unlike a conventional bit, which can be read repeatedly without altering its content, direct measurement of a quantum system typically causes the state to collapse before it can be determined. In other words, reading the information modifies it.

A new study with support from FAPESP proposes circumventing this problem by utilizing a unique property of a certain type of qubit called an “Andreev qubit.” This qubit produces an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum dynamics. This supercurrent would serve as a macroscopic indicator of the qubit’s state, enabling its reconstruction in a virtually non-destructive manner.

items.title: Disadvantages of Designating Mathematicians for AI Output Releases
items.summary:
[This is a guest post by the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence , crossposted from their site. This blog post was initially written in a different file format and converted using AI. — T.]

In our September 29 recommendations , we outlined an approach to the release of AI-generated mathematical output by AI labs. Since then, we have been asked by people from multiple labs and by several mathematicians about a specific aspect of the recommendations — that the development of human understanding following a release must remain organic and community led — and what it says about the question of the labs choosing specific mathematicians to participate in various ways in the release of their output. The purpose of this document is to clarify this point and to explain the reasoning behind our position on it. We welcome further feedback from the community and engagement with these arguments.

In some past releases an AI company has designated mathematicians to receive the output on a problem, often before anyone else. Those mathematicians then worked to uncover the ideas in the output, check them, develop them, and present them to the wider community. The appeal of this release model is easy to see: it puts expert eyes on the output early, can lead to a better initial public writeup, and gives each result a knowledgeable point of contact.

After consideration of many negative effects that this release plan has, however, we have come to the conclusion that on balance the disadvantages outweigh the advantages. This should in no way be construed as criticism of the mathematicians who have taken on such a role: they have acted in good faith and done valuable work. Nonetheless, we recommend that AI companies do not adopt this practice for future releases, for the reasons below.

Delayed or unequal access. In cases where designated mathematicians see material before everyone else, they get a head start on problems others may have worked on for years. Other mathematicians may have valuable contributions to make based on the material but may not have access to it, and may be dissuaded from working on it.

The remaining reasons apply even if all the material is released publicly at once.

Denied agency. The choice of who works to understand, check, and write up an important AI-generated result is consequential, both for those chosen and for the field, especially in the current period of transition when norms around credit for mathematical activities are in flux. If an AI company designates a particular mathematician to undertake or lead this task, it is to an extent making this decision for the community and denying it agency over its field of study. Further, this choice may discourage other mathematicians from contributing to the understanding of the results.

items.title: Vote! (Israeli edition)
items.summary:
Someone writing an article for the Israeli press about “people abroad who love Israel but might be worried” emailed me the following questions:

“1. What is something about Israel that you admire/appreciate over the years?

2. What are you worried the most about Israel these days?”

So I replied as follows:

“It’s hard to know where to start with either of your questions! But briefly:

Tiny Israel standing up for itself, against an often hostile and unjust world, is a huge part of what’s given me the self-confidence to stand up for myself in my own life. That was true even before I had visited Israel or spent significant time there, gazed across the desert at the still-clear ruins of the Roman siege of Masada, staggered overwhelmed out of Yad Vashem into the sunlight of Jerusalem, tasted the hummus or pomegranate juice or ice cream with blended fruit, befriended or had academic collaborations with dozens of Israelis, or married an Israeli woman.

My fear is merely the ‘obvious’ one — that, in response to the staggering hostility directed against the ‘Jew among the nations,’ Israel will become more and more belligerent, isolated, and right-wing. It will get demographically overwhelmed by those who don’t want to work or serve in the army, while hundreds of thousands of secular educated Israelis leave. It will be internally divided almost to the point of civil war. It will repudiate the liberal-democratic vision of Herzl and Ben-Gurion, of world-class universities and making the deserts bloom, for the swaggering, theocratic vision of Smotrich and Ben-Gvir, of chasing Palestinians from their olive groves. It will become more and more like the hateful caricature of itself that the anti-Israel people in the West always imagined. And then, having been internally weakened in all of these ways, it will finally be destroyed by its external enemies, who will never have rested the whole time, who never once wavered in their dream of a second Holocaust.

items.title: oai-math-revised: a community hub for revising OpenAI’s math write-ups
items.summary:
[This is a guest post by Abhinav Nellore , Johannes Schmitt , Soledad Villar , and Rachel Ward – T.]

OpenAI’s math write-ups at https://github.com/openai/math can be difficult to understand and can have incomplete citations.

https://github.com/mathcommunity/oai-math-revised/ seeks to be an inclusive effort to improve these write-ups, and the broader math community–students, postdocs, professors, and enthusiasts–is invited to participate.

The repo is browsable at https://mathcommunity.github.io/oai-math-revised/

We also invite the community to email mathcommunityadmin@gmail.com if they want to serve as admins/reviewers and for which categories from https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/overview.pdf they’d be appropriate for reviews.

items.title: Build Your Own Reasoning Model: A Full Video Course
items.summary:
I have written a lot about reasoning models here over the last two years on Ahead of AI, including a recent article on mechanisms to control reasoning effort levels in contemporary LLMs . Reasoning models are still as relevant as ever. In fact, almost all current-generation LLMs today are reasoning models or offer a reasoning mode.

For those who are interested in how reasoning models work, including inference scaling, reinforcement learning, and distillation, I wrote my recent Build Reasoning Model (From Scratch), which implements these from the ground up in PyTorch, which, in my experience, is still the best way to understand and learn how things really work.

Now, in the last few months, I also sat down and recorded accompanying lectures I wanted to share with you. So, below, you will find eight reasoning model-from-scratch coding videos (11 hours of content).

We start with a pre-trained LLM and implement methods to evaluate and improve it in Python and PyTorch. So, if you enjoyed my Coding LLMs from the Ground Up course last year, this is essentially the sequel (but you can also watch it without the prior course as a prerequisite).

I’m currently taking a short break and will be back soon with more exciting LLM research roundups next month. In the meantime, I hope you enjoy coding along!

How LLMs, reasoning models, and agents relate and fit together As a small side note, and since I often get asked how reasoning models relate to today’s AI agents, here’s a short section on this before getting started with the videos.

A reasoning model is essentially an upgrade from a conventional LLM, that is, adding more post-training via reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (and optionally inference scaling techniques) to make it more capable of solving more challenging problems. Classically, reasoning models are developed for math and code, but the capabilities can generalize to other problem domains as well.

items.title: Mehmet Sanliol (Evercore): Why quantum valuations hinge on 2030 revenue multiples and consolidation
items.summary:
Yuval Boger interviews Mehmet Sanliol, managing director at Evercore covering quantum technologies and semiconductors. They discuss how investors value public quantum companies, when private companies should consider IPOs or SPACs, and why consolidation may shape the next phase of the industry. Mehmet also shares his perspective on technical and market signals that could affect valuations, the outlook for quantum software, and the recent developments in quantum that caught his attention most.

items.title: Foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic
items.summary:
This paper studies foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic.

We provide an explicit description of all smooth foliations, linear and turbulent, and establish criteria for being $p$-closed.

We explicitly determine the moduli spaces of such foliations.

We give an application to the construction of $p$-closed foliations, with mild singularities, on Kummer $K3$-surfaces in positive characteristics.

items.title: Maximal Orbital Entanglement from Non-Interacting Fermions
items.summary:
Orbital rotations are used in quantum many-body physics and chemistry to reduce the complexity of quantum states by compressing their correlation into a small set of relevant orbitals. In striking contrast, quantum information processing strives for the opposite: orbitals that maximize entanglement as a resource.

Motivated by this, we prove that Slater determinants of $N$ fermions on a lattice of $d_A + d_B = d$ sites, although free of particle correlation, can carry up to $\min\{d_A, d_B, N, d-N\}$ ebits of orbital entanglement. Given enough particles and holes, this equals the maximum over all fermionic states.

For arbitrary free states, we derive the maximal orbital total correlation in closed form for all bipartitions, the finest partition, and all partitions of up to five sites, using new majorization relations for Hermitian matrices. Taken together, these results turn mean-field states, the starting point of most many-body methods in physics and chemistry, into a viable resource for quantum information processing.

items.title: Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions
items.summary:
Quantum-centric supercomputing (QCSC) approaches, such as sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), combine quantum processors with high-performance computers (HPC), offering a promising route toward solving challenging electronic structure problems. However, implementation of QCSC approaches to large active space calculations is constrained by the associated number of qubits, deep quantum circuits, sampling cost, and large-scale Hamiltonian diagonalization.

To overcome these limitations, we introduce a distributed QCSC framework that decomposes complex molecular problems into parallel sub-problems requiring fewer qubits, shallower circuits, and reduced shot budgets. A physically motivated, two-step aggregation scheme then reconstructs the global solution: first, a computational bit assignment strategy optimizes a cost function to appropriately map local bit indices to global ones, yielding a mapped tensor product state (MTPS); second, an inter-fragment correlation recovery module restores missing cross-fragment interactions.

Herein, we employ a multi-layered generative machine learning architecture, starting with utilizing the recently proposed physics-informed generative SQD (PIGen-SQD) as a distributed QCSC solver, followed by a secondary generative module to model configuration distributions and identify dominant sectors of the global Hilbert space. For water and formamide dimers, our method achieves up to $95\%$ reduction in the diagonalization dimension while enhancing energy accuracy by an order of magnitude over conventional SQD.

Furthermore, application to the water hexamer ($\mathrm{(H_2O)_6}$) cage successfully decomposes a 120-qubit problem into six 20-qubit monomeric subsystems, and stitches the monomers under a dimeric approximation, demonstrating excellent agreement with the reference classical methods.

items.title: The Verra involution on special cubic fourfolds
items.summary:
We present a detailed study of the Hodge theory, geometry and derived categories of Verra fourfolds, and their relationship with twisted K3 surfaces and cubic fourfolds. We classify Brauer classes of Verra type on K3 surfaces of degree 2, and use this to derive an explicit counting formula for Fourier--Mukai partners of a large class of Verra fourfolds.

We develop the basic theory of cohomology of Verra fourfolds and apply it to prove a derived Torelli theorem for a large class of Verra fourfolds. As an application, we prove that L-equivalent Verra fourfolds in this class are Fourier--Mukai partners, and conjecture that this implication holds for all Verra fourfolds.

We then give a construction of cubic fourfolds birational to Verra fourfolds. The construction yields examples of cubic and Verra fourfolds whose associated twisted K3 surfaces have non-trivial Brauer classes.

Therefore, these fourfolds are expected to be irrational.

items.title: Low-frustration block encodings by patch routing
items.summary:
Block-encoding has emerged as a core primitive in many quantum algorithms, including quantum simulation. In this work, we design efficient and extensible methods for generating low-frustration block encodings of frustrated lattice Hamiltonians built from repeated local interaction patches through a technique we call "patch routing".

We construct block encodings for a full Hamiltonian by first block-encoding a small local patch and then using a SWAP-style routing network to coherently apply the local patch encoding across the lattice. The expensive, local block-encoding cost is paid only once per query and is independent of lattice size, whereas the comparatively inexpensive routing network grows linearly with the lattice size, dominating at large sizes.

Our method allows for a hierarchical structure in which larger patches can be block-encoded with small normalization factors, albeit at a higher (local, non-extensive) block-encoding cost, thereby reducing overall query complexity in an algorithm. We exploit symmetries and algebraic structures in local interactions to construct efficient block encodings, and we apply these techniques to the Heisenberg, Fermi-Hubbard, and honeycomb spin-liquid models.

For a $120\times 120$ square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model near maximal frustration ($J_2/J_1=0.4-0.6$), our methods result in a $15-17\times$ reduction in the leading $T$ cost per qubitized-QPE run (ignoring initial state preparation and overlap) relative to prior state-of-the-art Pauli LCU constructions. Corresponding reductions are approximately $3\times$ for the $120\times120$ Fermi-Hubbard model at half-filling.

For time evolution of the honeycomb spin-liquid model on $120\times120$ unit cells, the leading cost is reduced by $5\times$. Our framework provides a systematic way forward for larger and more accurate fault-tolerant simulations of real-world quantum systems.

items.title: Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
items.summary:
Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) is conventionally used to probe elementary excitations and correlations in quantum materials. Here, we propose an interferometric RIXS protocol that instead creates entanglement between spatially separated regions of a solid-state material.

An incident X-ray photon is coherently split by a beam splitter into two arms illuminating opposite ends of a sample. Recombining the scattered photons at a second beam splitter and detecting an energy-selected photon then projects the material into a coherent superposition of excitations at the two ends.

This protocol is the X-ray, solid-state analogue of the Duan-Lukin-Cirac-Zoller (DLCZ) heralding scheme. Using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes, we show that orthogonal and degenerate end excitations yield maximally entangled states.

We illustrate this mechanism in three models: (1) two decoupled sites yield a heralded Bell state. (2) An open tight-binding chain exhibits reflection-parity-dependent interference, providing a benchmark for the interferometer's coherence.

(3) A spin-1 Haldane (AKLT) chain yields an entangled pair of fractionalized edge spins. We also discuss practical considerations and challenges for realizing the protocol in X-ray experiments.

items.title: Rank 3 curve semistable Higgs bundles: the nilpotent case
items.summary:
A Higgs bundle on a smooth complex projective variety is curve semistable if its pullback to every smooth projective curve is semistable.

A 2008 conjecture asserts that this is equivalent to slope semistability for some polarization plus vanishing discriminant.

One direction is known, the converse holds in rank two, and Huang recently gave a rank-four counterexample.

We prove the conjecture for rank three nilpotent Higgs bundles in any dimension.

We treat separately the two possible cases: if the Higgs field $φ$ is nilpotent of order two, there is a divisorial component of a Higgs Grassmannian where nefness of the normalized tautological class forces the discriminant to vanish; otherwise, $φ$ is regular nilpotent, and then the canonical kernel flag, commutativity and Bogomolov's lemma on line subbundles of the cotangent bundle complete the proof.

items.title: Linear transformations of tropical matrices preserving individual values of the cyclicity index
items.summary:
The cyclicity index is used to study the periodic behavior of powers of tropical matrices.

It is determined by the structure of the critical subgraph of a matrix, which consists of the cycles with the largest average weight.

In this paper bijective linear transformations of tropical matrices that preserve an individual value $k\neq 2$ of this invariant are studied.

items.title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
items.summary:
Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to optimize code for performance. This practice often assumes that improvements in execution speed naturally translate into overall lower energy consumption. We challenge this assumption empirically by measuring whether performance-optimized code produced by LLM self-refinement pipelines is also energy-efficient relative to canonical human reference solutions, and whether the energy cost of the optimization process can be offset by subsequent execution-time savings.

We evaluate 11 open-source models across four decoding configurations on all 1,000 problems of EffiBench, a state-of-the-art performance benchmark, while collecting per-process, hardware-level energy measurements throughout. Inference energy spans 0.79 to 8.68 MJ across model-variant pairs, which is roughly equivalent to the energy of 250 to 2800 GPT-4.1 queries. Limiting the maximum number of output tokens has the largest impact, reducing energy use by up to 69% compared to the default configuration.

On the execution side, 42 of 44 configurations produce code that consumes more energy per problem than the canonical human reference, with overheads ranging from +4% to +886%. The two exceptions achieve only marginal gains, with break-even points on the order of 10^6 to 10^7 executions. Mixture-of-Experts architectures consume substantially less inference energy than equivalently-sized dense models without sacrificing correctness, making architectural choice a more consequential sustainability lever than decoding parameters.

Performance optimization and energy efficiency are not always aligned goals: LLM self-refinement consistently produces faster-seeking but energy-heavier code relative to what a human engineer would write. All artifacts are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23598170.

items.title: Fermion Scattering on Quantum Computers
items.summary:
Resonant scattering links particle interactions to the formation and decay of unstable excitations. We develop a hybrid quantum-computing framework to study these dynamics through fermion--antifermion collisions.

Our formulation of $(1+1)$-dimensional Yukawa theory encodes fermions in qubits and the scalar field in qumodes. We identify the operations needed for a photonic implementation and benchmark the dynamics with tensor-network simulations.

Near resonance, we resolve the build-up of a localised scalar excitation and the subsequent partial return of energy to the fermions. Enhanced entanglement accompanies this exchange.

Time-dependent correlator measurements reproduce the analytically predicted decay rate to a few percent precision, with energy scans exhibiting a resonance peak consistent with packet-averaged Breit--Wigner behaviour. These results establish a concrete scattering benchmark for hybrid quantum computers and demonstrate how local real-time observables can probe particle-resonance dynamics.

items.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
items.summary:
Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but its cost is dominated by autoregressive rollout generation, which can exceed 70% of training time. Existing speculative-decoding methods are poorly suited to this setting: model-based drafters consume scarce GPU memory and may become misaligned as the policy evolves, while existing model-free methods do not explicitly exploit repetition across training epochs.

We observe that recent rollouts of the same prompt provide a high-quality, self-updating draft source. Based on this insight, we propose NgramRL, a per-prompt n-gram drafter constructed from bounded recent rollout history.

NgramRL requires no auxiliary model, drafter training, or persistent GPU-resident drafter state, while target-model verification preserves the rollout distribution. To hide CPU cache lookup and scheduling, we further introduce an adaptive fan-out prefetcher that predicts likely verification outcomes (j, b), consisting of the accepted draft length j and target-emitted continuation token b.

A causal budget allocator concentrates prefetches on high-probability outcomes, while uncovered outcomes fall back to sequential lookup without changing committed tokens. Across two model families and three reasoning and structured-generation workloads, NgramRL commits 3.60-7.77 tokens per target-model forward in the warm-cache regime, up to 1.99x more than SuffixDecoding and 7.0x more than prompt-lookup decoding.

On Spider, the prefetcher covers 96.6% of Qwen3-8B outcomes at a candidate budget of 16 and improves measured rollout throughput by 1.38x over synchronous NgramRL, approaching its 1.40x overlap ceiling.

items.title: Hardware-Friendly Estimation of LCU-Based Expectation Values via Quantum-to-Classical Workload Shifting
items.summary:
Estimating the expectation value of an observable $O$ for a quantum state evolved under a general, possibly non-unitary, operator $A$ is a fundamental task in quantum simulation, chemistry, and variational algorithms. Existing linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) approaches implement $A$ on hardware, requiring ancilla qubits, controlled unitaries and, in randomized variants, fresh circuit executions for every Monte Carlo sample.

These costs are prohibitive on NISQ and early fault-tolerant devices. We propose HERMES (Hardware-Efficient Reusable Measurements for Estimating LCU-based expectation valueS), which moves the processing of $A$ entirely to the classical domain.

Expanding $A$ and $O$ in the Pauli basis and sampling pairs of Pauli terms classically, HERMES rewrites $μ= \mathrm{Tr}(OAρA^{\dagger})/\mathrm{Tr}(AρA^{\dagger})$ as a ratio of weighted sums of Pauli expectation values on the unmodified state $ρ$, with no ancillas, controlled unitaries, or quantum implementation of $A$. A two-level measurement reduction scheme (Pauli deduplication and commuting-group partitioning) bounds the number of distinct measurement settings independently of the sample count, unlike randomized LCU methods whose circuit executions grow linearly with it.

On ground-state energy estimation of $\mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{LiH}$ via imaginary-time evolution, HERMES matches or beats Pauli single-ancilla LCU baseline using shallow circuits with no two-qubit gates beyond state preparation under qubit-wise commuting grouping. It is also more robust to noise and completes a noisy $\mathrm{LiH}$ simulation infeasible for the baseline, at the cost of classical overhead growing with the number of Pauli terms in $A$.

items.title: Modular optical fault-tolerant quantum computation via an interface between verified resources and online logical operations
items.summary:
We introduce a factory--processor interface architecture for modular optical fault-tolerant quantum computation that separates code-dependent encoded-resource preparation from reusable online logical processing on a common Gaussian optical processor.

Beyond encoded resources, the interface specifies logical outputs, code-to-mode mapping, measurement roles, frame updates, verification records, and resource-injection boundaries.

As a concrete realization, we combine an offline verified Bell-resource factory based on a recursively concatenated $C_4$ code with physical Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) qubits with an online time-domain measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) processor.

Under the specified additive-displacement-noise model and fixed postselection policy, simulations support the finite-level logical Bell-error ordering $P_5

items.title: Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials for permutations with $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and Irreducible Singular Locus
items.summary:
We determine the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ for permutations $w$ such that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and the Schubert variety $X_w$ has irreducible singular locus.

Let $h=h(w)$ be the minimum height $w(a)-w(d)$ of a $3412$-occurrence in $w$ at positions $a 1$.

This proves the irreducible singular locus case of a 2009 conjecture of Billey and Weed.

items.title: $G_0$ of complete split toric varieties
items.summary:
We compute the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves for complete split toric surfaces having a smooth 2-dimensional cone in its fan.

We show that it is free abelian, of rank equal to the number of rays in the fan.

We give a partial generalization of this to all complete split toric varieties.

items.title: Structure and Exact Certification of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions
items.summary:
We study the structure and exact certification of nonnegative tensor decompositions supplied through rational factor matrices. Every failure of minimality or essential uniqueness contains an irreducible positive exchange between $p$ supplied terms and $q$ competing terms.

A dimension count based on the Lovitz--Petrov splitting theorem bounds the effective order of such an exchange, the sum over the modes of the joint factor-span dimension minus one, by $p+q-2$, and this bound is attained at every supplied length $R\ge2$. After eliminating ambient-row variables by the Farkas lemma, the resulting semialgebraic systems have fewer than $2R^2$ real variables.

For input bit length $L$, this gives a deterministic $G(R)L^{O(R^2)}$-time algorithm that computes the nonnegative rank and an exact minimum-length decomposition, decides minimality and essential uniqueness, and returns exact witnesses when either property fails. The exponent is independent of the tensor order and the mode dimensions.

For Lebesgue moment tensors, positive quadrature determines the nonnegative rank and the uniqueness behavior, and some rational length-$R$ inputs force a common field of degree at least $\lfloor R/2\rfloor!$ for any exact minimum-length output. As an illustration, an implementation resolves all 114 instances left inconclusive by earlier positive-scattering criteria, of which 95 are minimal and essentially unique and 19 are minimal but nonunique.

items.title: On quasi-Albanese morphisms for log canonical Calabi-Yau pairs II
items.summary: Centering on quasi-Albanese morphisms, we prove several structural theorems for Calabi-Yau pairs.

items.title: Large profinite genus and extensions in Bestvina-Brady groups
items.summary:
We construct the first examples of uncountable families of residually finite duality groups of type $FP$, all of which have isomorphic profinite completions, while being pairwise not quasi-isometric.

To establish these finiteness properties, we prove conjectures of Leary regarding groups of deck transformations of certain cubical branched covers being residually finite and virtually special.

The main new tool is a strong separability result for Bestvina-Brady groups, allowing the extension of any finite quotient of many Bestvina-Brady subgroups to a finite quotient of the whole group.

This gives a finite version of the congruence extension property, which we also establish for the same group pairs.

items.title: IAS applications for membership in the school of mathematics
items.summary:
The IAS has opened its application page for its membership program for the upcoming year. This by itself would be unremarkable — the program does this every year — but there is an additional statement included in the announcement:

We realize that applying to positions in the current environment is stressful. To help alleviate this, the School of Mathematics offers applicants the option to submit research statement based only on already conducted research. It would be helpful if such a statement would be focused on a few select projects (in most cases up to three) and not a wide ranging list.

I would expect other departments and institutes advertising positions this year to adopt similar guidance. (See also a recent report from a working group making similar recommendations in the area of theoretical computer science.)

Readers are also invited to post links to other job openings in mathematics in the comments.

items.title: Quantum Machine Learning in Medical Imaging: A Primer for Radiologists
items.summary:
Deep learning has transformed radiology, but the computational cost of training and deploying modern models is outpacing what classical hardware can support. Quantum computing has been proposed as one response to this bottleneck: an n-qubit system can represent $2^n$ states simultaneously, although practical speedups require efficient algorithms, data encoding, and measurement strategies rather than superposition alone.

This review introduces radiologists to five core quantum concepts, qubits, superposition, entanglement, quantum gates, and quantum circuits, and to the superconducting, trapped-ion, and photonic hardware platforms that define the current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. We then summarize the quantum machine learning architectures most often applied to medical imaging (quantum support vector machines, quantum neural networks, variational quantum circuits, and quantum convolutional neural networks) and quantum image representations such as the flexible representation of quantum images (FRQI) and the novel enhanced quantum representation (NEQR).

Reported applications include brain tumor classification and segmentation on MRI, pneumonia detection on chest radiographs, skin and breast lesion classification, CT and PET reconstruction, and ultrasound denoising. Nearly all published systems are hybrid quantum-classical pipelines evaluated on small, downsampled benchmark datasets or simulators, and clinical deployment is not yet feasible.

We conclude with current limitations and translational priorities for radiology.

items.title: The restricted Hurwitz action on cameral decompositions of Coxeter elements
items.summary:
Given a dual Coxeter system (W, T) of rank n, the Hurwitz action of the braid group on the reduced T-decompositions of a Coxeter element is transitive.

When we choose a geometric representation of W, the reflections with respect to the n walls of one given chamber form a generating set S that we call cameral.

An ordering of S is called a cameral decomposition and the product a cameral Coxeter element, which depends only on the quiver obtained by orienting the Coxeter diagram with vertices S according to the ordering.

We show that the reduced decompositions of a cameral Coxeter elements for which the underlying set S satisfies that (W, S ) is a Coxeter system, are necessarily cameral, and we count the number of chambers from which a cameral Coxeter element can be obtained.

We show that one can go through all these chambers using the restricted Hurwitz action on the set of cameral decompositions, which is generated by transpositions of adjacent commuting reflections and by the Garside element δ of the dual Garside structure, which acts by a quiver mutation of the orientation of the Coxeter diagram.

items.title: The totally nonnegative wonderful compactification of G is a ball
items.summary:
Let $\overline{G}$ denote the wonderful compactification of a semisimple algebraic group $G$ of adjoint type.

We use contractive flows to show that the totally nonnegative part of every $G \times G$ orbit closure of $\overline{G}$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball.

In particular, the totally nonnegative part of $\overline{G}$ is homeomorphic to a closed ball.

items.title: A genus-two spectral curve of the Riemann $Ξ$-function: Real Structure and Certified Arithmetic Separation of Periods
items.summary:
We associate a compact genus-two real spectral core with a transverse logarithmic-derivative discriminant of the Riemann $Ξ$-function. Directed interval arithmetic certifies its branch geometry, a real $P_{\mathrm{III}}(D_6)$ scalar-normal-form realization, and associated Kummer and Shioda--Inose models.

Zero-action resonance reduces to rationality of two real period ratios. Their certified heat motion yields generic local nonresonance and Diophantine separation, while explicit Farey windows impose denominator barriers of $1{,}036{,}003$ and $140{,}769$ throughout $|κ|\le3\times10^{-10}$ in the heat time $κ$.

Fixed-point irrationality and exact Picard rank remain open. The heat tangent differs from the matched fixed-exponent isomonodromic direction, but admits a local moving-exponent curve lift.

Separately, a reciprocal-head canopy certificate combined with published finite-RH and rectangular time-barrier verifications bounds the de Bruijn--Newman constant by $Λ\le433/2500=0.1732$ without a QRH assumption. These local arithmetic and global analytic results share a phase--transverse bridge; no equivalence between core nonresonance and RH is asserted.

items.title: Realizable Cohomology Classes of Dihedral and Generalized Quaternion Groups
items.summary:
We compute the Chern classes of irreducible representations for the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ and the generalized quaternion groups $Q_{2^n}$.

Utilizing these computations, we investigate whether every even-dimensional class in the integral group cohomology of these families can be realized as a Chern class of some complex representation.

It turns out that this realizability question answers in the affirmative for the generalized quaternion groups.

In contrast, it turns out that the answer for dihedral groups is erratic.

items.title: The Lie algebra structure of $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ for blocks with a normal defect group
items.summary:
It is an open question whether the Lie algebra $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ of a block of a finite group algebra $kG$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of prime characteristic $p$ is simple only if the block is nilpotent with an elementary abelian defect group of order at least $3$.

We show this to be the case if $B$ has a normal abelian defect group.

Another open question is whether $\mathrm{HH}^1(kS_n)$ is a solvable Lie algebra, where $S_n$ denotes a symmetric group on $n$ letters.

We give some general solvability criteria for $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ of blocks $B$ with a normal defect group, and, making use of results of Chuang-Kessar and Chuang-Rouquier, we deduce that if $B$ is a block of a symmetric group algebra with an abelian defect group, then $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is solvable.

items.title: Governor Hochul Announces New Study Highlighting New York’s Position as a National Leader in Quantum Technology
items.summary:
Insider Brief

A state-commissioned study ranks New York second nationally in quantum-related businesses, research groups and patents, identifying greater coordination as an opportunity to accelerate commercialization.

New York has committed $360 million to quantum development, including $300 million for a Stony Brook research hub and $60 million for up to four regional commercialization hubs.

The study estimates these investments could support $2.3 billion to $5 billion in economic activity and 7,200 to 10,100 job-years through 2036.

PRESS RELEASE — Governor Kathy Hochul today announced the release of a comprehensive study of New York State’s quantum technology landscape, finding that the Empire State ranks second nationally in quantum-related businesses, research groups and patents. Commissioned by Empire State Development’s Division of Science, Technology and Innovation (NYSTAR), the study highlights New York’s position as a national leader in the emerging industry and identifies opportunities to strengthen collaboration, accelerate commercialization and support future economic growth.

“New York is building the foundation for the next generation of technological breakthroughs, and quantum technology represents an enormous opportunity for our economy,” Governor Hochul said. “With world-class research institutions, advanced manufacturing capabilities and a growing network of innovative businesses, we have the tools to lead this emerging industry. Our $360 million investment will help turn that potential into progress, bringing new technologies to market, attracting private investment and creating good-paying jobs across New York State.”

Empire State Development President, CEO and Commissioner Hope Knight said, “Under Governor Hochul’s leadership, New York is making strategic investments to lead the next generation of technological innovation. This study confirms that our state has the research institutions, manufacturing capabilities and industry expertise needed to compete in the growing quantum economy. By connecting these strengths and supporting commercialization, we’re positioning New York to attract investment, create good-paying jobs and turn groundbreaking research into real economic opportunity.”

items.title: Rank identifications in join-meet ideals of thin distributive lattices
items.summary:
Let $L$ be a thin distributive lattice of rank $m+1$, and let $I_L$ be its join-meet ideal in the polynomial ring $S_L$.

For $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$, let $J_A$ be the ideal obtained from $I_L$ by identifying, for every $i\in A$, the variables of the two elements of $L$ of rank $i$.

We prove that $J_A$ is prime if and only if $A$ contains no turning rank and does not contain both ranks adjacent to a turning rank.

In this case, $S_L/J_A$ is the toric ring obtained from Hibi's parametrization of the Hibi ring of $L$ by identifying suitable pairs of variables, and for an arbitrary $A$ we describe the saturation of $J_A$ as a lattice ideal.

items.title: Split Frobenius Groups, Equational Domains, $\mathfrak{X}T$- and $CS\mathfrak{X}$-groups
items.summary:
We investigate conditions under which a semidirect product $G=HN$, and in particular a restricted wreath product, is an equational domain.

For a variety of groups $\X$, we study semidirect products of $\XT$-groups (groups where $\langle A, B\rangle \in\X$ for any two $\X$-subgroups $A$ and $B$ with nontrivial intersection) and $\CSX$-groups (groups where all maximal $\X$-subgroups are malnormal).

We pay particular attention to split Frobenius groups and investigate conditions under which such groups are $\XT$- or $\CSX$-groups.

items.title: InferSlice: A Reference Architecture for SLO-driven LLM Inference over a Telco Wide-Area Network
items.summary:
LLM inference is increasingly deployed as a core service for enterprise and interactive applications, but sovereignty, compliance, latency and resource-locality requirements can limit the suitability of centralised cloud deployments. Telco operators offer geographically distributed compute and network infrastructure for addressing these constraints.

However, existing LLM serving frameworks are designed for tightly coupled data centres and provide limited support for coordinating geographically distributed and heterogeneous resources. We present InferSlice, a reference architecture for Service-Level Objective (SLO)-driven LLM inference over a telco infrastructure, integrating network slicing, GPU partitioning, elastic serving and observability.

Led by BT in collaboration with the University of Bristol and NVIDIA, and realised on the JOINER UK national-scale wide-area network (WAN), InferSlice is evaluated on service differentiation across tiers, elastic scale-out, client-edge bandwidth as a bottleneck, and the reach of tensor, pipeline, data parallelism, and prefill/decode disaggregation over the WAN. Our results show that, on a general-purpose telco network, tiers yield distinct latency-throughput regimes, and weight streaming shortens scale-out time.

Replication is placement-insensitive but memory-bound; pipeline parallelism tolerates near- and mid-cross-site hops, while tensor parallelism and disaggregation fail beyond a single subnet hop. We share practical insights from operating SLO-driven inference on a telco network, lessons learned and open questions, and hope to encourage further research on distributed and heterogeneous LLM inference systems.

items.title: Trace-distance characterization of recurrent pairwise synchronization in cavity-coupled superconducting qubits
items.summary:
We theoretically investigate recurrent pairwise synchronization in three super?conducting qubits coupled to a common single-mode microwave cavity. The qubits interact indirectly through the cavity field and are driven by a coher?ent microwave field.

We obtain the coherent dynamics in the dressed-state basis and quantify pairwise synchronization by the trace distance between reduced single-qubit density matrices. The trace-distance dynamics exhibit oscillatory wave-packet structures, with low-trace-distance regions identifying finite syn?chronization windows.

An envelope-threshold procedure is introduced to extract the representative duration of these windows. By varying the middle-qubit coupling strength and the relative coupling ratio of the outer qubits, we con?struct a parameter-dependent map of the synchronization-window duration.

The duration decreases rapidly with increasing relative outer-qubit coupling and becomes weakly dependent on the middle-qubit coupling in the stronger-coupling regime. These results provide a reduced-state-based characterization of coherent collective dynamics in multiqubit circuit-QED systems.

items.title: Restricted isometries in finite-dimensional $\ell^p$-spaces
items.summary:
For $d,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq1}$ and $p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$, we characterize all linear maps $s\colon\ell_d^p\to\ell_n^p$ for which there is $E\subseteq X_d$ such that $\|s(ξ)\|_p=\|ξ|_E\|_p$ for every $ξ\in\ell_d^p$. We call these maps \emph{restricted isometries}.

Our Lamperti-type theorem gives a unique description of each such operator using a set transformation, a positive amplitude function, and a unimodular phase function. In particular, it includes noninjective and nonsurjective operators, even when the dimensions differ.

We further characterize restricted isometries between finite $\ell^p$-spaces with arbitrary positive atomic weights. Applications include formulas counting set transformations and uniform restricted isometries, as well as a geometric description of all restricted isometries with fixed column supports.

items.title: The Compendium of Super-Quadratic Computational Quantum Advantages
items.summary:
This compendium presents a structured collection of computational problems with credible prospects for realizing meaningful quantum advantage, focused on describing problem characteristics rather than specific algorithms.

It is intended for non-quantum researchers and practitioners with strong computational backgrounds, particularly domain experts, seeking to assess the relevance of quantum methods to real-world problems.

The compendium focuses on enumerating core problems for which there is good evidence that a quantum computer can realize more than a quadratic speedup in offline non-relativized time-complexity (e.g., as opposed to in oracular settings, streaming models, or communication advantages).

Entries characterize the structural constraints that real-world instances must satisfy to realize those advantages in practice.

The intention is to provide a reference that can be leveraged to connect quantum algorithms to practical use cases.

items.title: Deformations of cohomology classes and spectral sequences
items.summary:
We study spectral sequences as an obstruction theory to deforming cohomology classes via the Rees construction. A filtered complex is interpreted as an equivariant family over the affine line, in which higher spectral sequence differentials arise as obstructions to lifting cohomology classes through infinitesimal neighborhoods of the special fibre.

This leads to various geometric and module-theoretic degeneration criteria. We give various applications to $\mathrm{Ext}$ spectral sequences for complex Lagrangians and the formality results of Melani-Rubió amongst others.

For double complexes, we revisit the Khovanov-Qi decomposition on the Rees side and introduce a two-parameter Rees construction over the affine plane. The higher differentials of the two associated spectral sequences correspond to torsion modules supported on the thickened coordinate axes.

We obtain degeneration criteria in terms of these modules and an intrinsic characterisation of the $\partial\bar\partial$-lemma.

items.title: Affine and cyclotomic Brauer categorification via $\imath$-Kac--Moody $2$-categories: the integral type $\operatorname{AIII}$ case
items.summary:
Continuing our work on the half-integral case, we construct generalized nilpotent $2$-representations of the integral quasi-split type $\operatorname{AIII}$ $\imath$-Kac--Moody $2$-category from affine Brauer actions with dot spectrum exactly $\mathbb Z$ on locally Schurian $\mathbb C$-linear categories. Conversely, nilpotent $2$-representations on such categories yield affine Brauer actions with spectrum contained in $\mathbb Z$.

At the fixed vertex $0$, we directly define corrected generators and verify the nil-Brauer and mixed relations. For $\mathbf u$-admissible integral parameters at arbitrary positive level, we prove an isomorphism between the locally unital algebras of the cyclotomic Brauer category and a cyclotomic quotient of the principal $2$-representation.

This gives compatible $\mathbb Z$-gradings on the category and its endomorphism algebras, providing a Brauer analogue of the graded realization of type $A$ cyclotomic Hecke algebras. Over algebraically closed fields of odd characteristic $p$, we also obtain both constructions with spectrum contained in $\mathbb F_p$, for the mixed affine datum restricted to its spectral weight subgroup.

items.title: Noetherian local rings without perfectoid towers
items.summary:
Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$.

We prove that if a $p$-torsionfree ring $R$, defined by homogeneous equations over $W(k)$, admits a perfectoid tower arising from $(R,(p))$, then its special fiber is $F$-liftable.

We also give explicit examples admitting no such tower, including examples with $F$-liftable special fibers.

items.title: Classical Pre-Training of Large Shallow Parametrized Quantum Circuits through Pauli Propagation and deployment on Quantum Hardware
items.summary:
Scaling parametrized quantum circuits to a larger number of qubits is a central challenge in Quantum Machine Learning: gradient estimation via the parameter-shift rule quickly becomes prohibitively expensive, while gradient-free optimizers offer limited convergence guarantees. We apply the Pauli propagation framework to a broad class of Quantum Machine Learning problems in which the loss is expressed as a function of expectation values of the circuit's observables, while keeping the relevant quantity of interest, such as the quantum state or its samples, classically intractable to compute.

By propagating the observables backward through the circuit, we obtain an explicit parametric expression for the loss that can be minimized entirely on classical hardware. We also present complementary strategies to make propagation tractable at large scale, including weight-based and degree-based truncations and pruning heuristics.

We demonstrate the approach on two benchmarks run on 64-qubit circuits: Variational Quantum Eigensolver on a two-dimensional Ising model, and training of a discrete-type generative model for binary images. In both cases, the classically pre-trained parameters are deployed on the IBM quantum processor ibm_berlin.

For generative learning, we additionally show that the circuits considered here require substantially fewer parametrized gates than IQP-style ansätze, reducing transpilation overhead and making deployment on current quantum hardware feasible.

items.title: Biderivations of Null-Filiform and Filiform Zinbiel Algebras
items.summary:
A biderivation of an algebra is a bilinear map which is a derivation in each argument. We describe all biderivations of finite-dimensional complex null-filiform and filiform Zinbiel algebras.

For the n-dimensional null-filiform algebra, every biderivation is determined by an arbitrary value at its generating pair; the space of biderivations has dimension n and consists entirely of symmetric maps. For the three standard filiform families, we give explicit bases and determine their symmetric and skew-symmetric parts.

We also treat all filiform algebras of dimensions at most four, including the exceptional families not covered by the classification in dimensions at least five. A three-dimensional algebra admits a three-dimensional space of skew-symmetric biderivations, two of which have values outside its annihilator.

Up to isomorphism, it is the unique complex filiform Zinbiel algebra with this property. The proofs use generators, annihilator-valued maps, a truncated polynomial model, and conformal endomorphisms of bilinear forms.

items.title: Finite stabilization, socle extensions, and Faith's conjecture
items.summary:
We give a length-two counterexample to the unrestricted product comparison in Bergman's Question 3.1, positive criteria for quasi-injective common modules, and a semidirect-product version of Question 3.2. For semiprimary right self-injective rings, the countable hull construction yields a cyclic two-layer witness, its Baer class, and an opposite-side extension obstruction.

We apply this construction over the square-zero ring of the counterexample. The hull quotient of a countable sum of injectives is the endomorphism space modulo finite-rank maps, and computes the full socle-radical defect of a countable product of the regular module.

This gives a second counterexample with free cyclic family factors. The original length-two product embeds its defect in the same quotient through an explicit intersection, and all associated extension classes arise from one specified Baer class.

The general Faith conjecture remains unresolved.

items.title: Jacobian layers and higher Milnor sequences: rigidity, stabilization, and log-concavity
items.summary:
Let $f$ be an isolated hypersurface singularity and let $J(f)$ be its Jacobian ideal. We study the higher Milnor numbers $μ_k(f)=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal O_n/\mathfrak m^kJ(f).$ Our main result concerns an ordinary semi-homogeneous singularity $f=f_r+f_{r+1}+\cdots$, where the projective hypersurface defined by $f_r$ is smooth. We prove that $μ_k(f)=μ_k(f_r) \qquad\text{for every }k\geq0.$ This gives the equal-weight case of a conjecture of Shi, Yau, and Zuo.

The main algebraic input is the common-order case of the Valabrega--Valla criterion. From it, we obtain the graded Jacobian module and the exact intersection formula. As a consequence, we obtain a closed formula for $μ_k$ and determine the sharp stabilization index of $\mathfrak m^kJ(f)$.

We also determine the optimal uniform range in which the Tjurina formula holds for all ordinary semi-homogeneous germs with fixed $n$ and $r$. We next consider the log-concavity property. For ordinary semi-homogeneous singularities, the higher Milnor sequence has an initial log-convex part and a log-concave tail.

For an arbitrary isolated hypersurface singularity in $n\geq2$ variables, both the higher Milnor and higher Tjurina sequences are eventually strictly log-concave. In the plane curve case, we prove that the log-concavity defects change sign at most once, and we characterize the sequences which are log-concave at every positive index. Finally, we give examples showing that the higher Milnor sequence does not determine the contact-equivalence class.

items.title: LYNX - A trapped-ion quantum information processor
items.summary:
We introduce LYNX, a quantum information processor based on trapped $^{40}$Ca$^+$ ions. It utilizes up to 31 qubits with all-to-all connectivity.

We characterize the system performance using rigorous benchmarks, such as randomized benchmarking (RB), GHZ state fidelity estimates, and quantum volume (QV) tests. The LYNX processor shows average 1-qubit gate errors of $8(5)\times 10^{-5}$ tested via standard RB in a 24-qubit register.

An average 2-qubit gate error in a 24-qubit register of $2.84(8)\times 10^{-3}$ is demonstrated using interleaved RB. Furthermore, the device passes QV tests using up to 15 qubits which corresponds to a quantum volume of QV$=2^{15}$.

items.title: Guest Post: Quantum Computing’s Next Phase May Be Driven by Compounding Breakthroughs
items.summary:
Guest Post by Liam Wang COO, Logical Qubit Technology.

The World Economic Forum’s Quantum Economy Day 2026 was held in Geneva, Switzerland, on October 13–14. Logical Qubit Technology attended as the only quantum computing company representing China. The company’s Chief Operating Officer, Liam Wang, joined business executives, researchers, and representatives of international organizations from around the world to discuss the global development of quantum computing.

This June, I took part in a World Economic Forum discussion on global quantum science and technology development at the Summer Davos meeting in Dalian. Representing the company again at Quantum Economy Day 2026 in Geneva gave me a close-up view of how quantum computing is developing in other countries and regions.

What Is Everyone Talking About?

My first and most immediate impression: China and other countries share many of the same concerns about this industry — how to persuade policymakers, capital, and industry to commit more resources to quantum computing; which application scenarios will see the first breakthroughs; how geopolitics continues to shape the global industry (supply chain security, the setting of global quantum standards, and so on); how to broaden quantum computing’s social reach, steadily moving beyond academia into industry and the wider public; and how the convergence of quantum computing and AI will unfold, and what major opportunities that super-cycle will create.

Although the industry is still at an early stage, the overall mood among participants was optimistic . AI was the most common point of comparison: since ChatGPT launched in November 2022, the pace of progress in large AI models has exceeded almost everyone’s expectations. Quantum computing is likely to follow a similar logic.

Of course, at this stage, quantum computing still has to be viewed pragmatically. Two terms came up most frequently in the discussions: “use case” and “geopolitics.”

items.title: Schur--Weyl duality for coideal subalgebras of quantum affine superalgebras of type $A$
items.summary: We extend the results of \cite{FLLLWW20} to the super setting. More precisely, we define two families of coideal sub-superalgebras of quantum affine superalgebras of type $A$, called $\jmath$- and $\imath$-quantum affine superalgebras respectively, and establish Schur--Weyl duality between them and affine Hecke algebras of type $C$.

items.title: IQM and Telefónica Plan Quantum Computer for Madrid University
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Telefónica and IQM Quantum Computers plan to install the first quantum computer in Spain’s Community of Madrid at the Technical University of Madrid (UPM) before the end of 2026.

The IQM Spark system is designed for research, education and early-stage development, giving universities, hospitals, research centers and start-ups access to quantum hardware.

The project aims to build regional expertise, support the development of industry use cases and expand Madrid’s role in Europe’s quantum technology ecosystem.

PRESS RELEASE — Telefónica and IQM Quantum Computers, a global leader in superconducting quantum computing, have joined forces to deploy the first quantum computer in the Community of Madrid. The initiative will strengthen the region’s scientific and technological capabilities, while driving the development of real-world cases for companies across the Community of Madrid.

The IQM Spark quantum computer, an all-in-one solution specifically designed for research, education and early-stage development, will be installed at the Technical University of Madrid (UPM) before the end of 2026. It will enable universities, hospitals, research centers and start-ups, direct access to real quantum hardware to develop and test quantum algorithms and build the expertise needed to explore future use cases.

This will be the first quantum computer of its kind in the Community of Madrid, significantly increasing the region’s capacity to develop quantum capabilities locally and through hands-on experience. The computer will join the other two quantum computers provided by Telefónica and IQM to CESGA (Galician Supercomputing Centre).

items.title: Reflection groups on smooth projective threefolds
items.summary:
Let $Y$ be a smooth projective threefold with $H^2(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)=0$ and unobstructed deformations.

We define reflection groups $W_Y^{sm}$ and $W_Y^{big}$ canonically associated to $Y$, acting on the nef, resp. movable cone of a very general deformation of $Y$.

If $-K_Y$ is nef, we show that $\mathrm{Nef}(Y)\cap\mathrm{Big}(Y)$ (resp. $\overline{\mathrm{Mov}}(Y)\cap\mathrm{Big}(Y)$) is a fundamental domain for the action of the corresponding group on the big part of the generic cone.

This generalizes work of Wilson and Lutz on Calabi--Yau threefolds.

The group $W_Y^{big}$ recovers and gives a deformation-theoretic explanation for the Weyl group action on divisor classes of point blowups of $\mathbb P^3$ studied by Dolgachev--Ortland and Mukai.

items.title: Quantum Secret Sharing from CSS qLDPC Codes: Computable Access Structures, Accessible Logical Dimension, and Topology-Aware Network Cost
items.summary:
Quantum secret sharing (QSS) schemes can be constructed from quantum error-correcting codes, but characterizing their access structures and implementation costs becomes challenging for finite-length, high-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes. We develop an exact computational framework for QSS induced by CSS qLDPC codes.

The framework characterizes authorized, forbidden, and intermediate coalitions using restricted parity-check matrices and binary linear algebra, and introduces the accessible logical dimension \(κ(A)\), defined through the symplectic rank of locally supported logical classes, to refine the characterization of intermediate coalitions. We further incorporate physical network constraints through separate Tanner-incidence, Steiner-routing, and scheduling-depth costs, and treat the partitioning of physical qubits into participants as an explicit design variable.

Numerical experiments on four CSS qLDPC codes verify the predicted complement duality and monotonicity properties and show substantial variation in access transitions and network costs. For the codes studied, the bivariate bicycle instance exhibits the sharpest transition, while network embedding costs vary by more than an order of magnitude across physical topologies.

We also show that participant partitioning can substantially improve block-level security and reconstruction thresholds. These results provide a practical bridge between the algebraic structure of CSS qLDPC codes, the graded accessibility of quantum secrets, and the physical constraints of networked QSS implementations.

items.title: Associative Lifts of CW Semigroups
items.summary:
Every nonempty connected finite-dimensional CW topological semigroup admits a continuous associative multiplication on its universal cover that lifts the multiplication of the base.

Such a multiplication is unique up to a deck transformation: in fact, any two associative lifts are conjugate whenever they exist.

We show that the finite-dimensional hypothesis cannot be dropped in general: a connected, countable, infinite-dimensional CW topological semigroup is constructed for which continuous lifts of multiplication exist, but none is associative.

The counterexample has nonabelian fundamental group isomorphic to Thompson's group $F$.

Thus finite dimensionality is sufficient for associative lifting in the CW setting, whereas the unrestricted infinite-dimensional statement fails.

items.title: Motivic local density of isolated singularities of algebraic varieties
items.summary: The goal of this paper is to compute the motivic local density of an isolated singularity of an algebraic variety, in order to explain its link with algebraic multiplicity. We compute the density as the residue in 1 of a Zeta function associated to normalized local volumes and we use a resolution of the singularity to get the formula.

items.title: Quivers with Involutions and Shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$Quantum groups via Coulomb Branches
items.summary:
We give a formula for quasi-minuscule monopole operators in $K$-theoretic quantized Coulomb branch algebras of cotangent type.

We then study signed quivers with involutions, with orthogonal or symplectic gauge factors at the involution-fixed vertices.

We construct a GKLO-type homomorphism from the corresponding shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$quantum group to an algebra of $q$-difference operators and prove that it factors through the quantized Coulomb branch algebra.

These homomorphisms give geometric realizations of the shifted affine $\mathrm{i}$quantum groups in terms of dressed minuscule and quasi-minuscule monopole operators.

items.title: A New Characterisation of Selflessness
items.summary:
We characterise the existence of expectation-preserving embeddings of reduced amalgamated free product $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras into norm ultrapowers of the first factor, fixing its diagonal copy pointwise, in terms of complementary compression relations on Hilbert space ultrapowers.

This yields new characterisations of Robert's notion of selflessness, selfless inclusions, and relative selflessness with respect to conditional expectations.

We also characterise Ozawa's notion of complete selflessness, including its extension to inclusions.

We then illustrate the usefulness of these characterisations by establishing complete selflessness for suitable reduced (amalgamated) free products, free Araki--Woods $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras, certain Hecke $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras, and $q$-Gaussian $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-algebras.

Finally, we obtain dynamical characterisations of (complete) $\mathrm{C}^\ast$-selflessness of discrete groups and establish relative selflessness for suitable reduced crossed products.

items.title: Optimality of finite field dimension expanders
items.summary:
We show that random tuples of matrices over a finite field are uniform dimension expanders for every expansion coefficient below the optimal one, using elementary counting arguments.

The same holds for the optimal coefficient along a set of dimensions of density 1.

By contrast, along Fibonacci dimensions random pairs of matrices fail to be optimal dimension expanders with probability bounded away from zero.

items.title: Meromorphic approximation of holomorphic maps into algebraically elliptic projective varieties
items.summary:
We show that holomorphic maps from a neighborhood of a compact set in a Stein space to an algebraically elliptic smooth projective variety can be approximated by meromorphic maps, provided that the map extends continuously to the whole space and the compact set is convex with respect to a submonoid of the Picard group.

The proof uses algebraic sprays and their polynomial lifts to affine cones, which we call conic lifts.

Rational sprays, which generalize algebraic sprays, extend the result to maps avoiding the exceptional set of a rational spray.
